events.content:
I implemented the Dashboard using the same pattern as `getParallelData()` in `app/page.tsx`. Type-checking passes and `next build` succeeds. I haven't run it against real `/api/*` endpoints, because the repo doesn't have any.

**`app/Dashboard.tsx`**
- `getDashboardData()` fetches all three endpoints at the same time with `Promise.all`. If anything fails, it falls back to mock data, just as the existing helper does.
- The component shows analytics (page views and visitors), a list of notifications, and settings (theme and language).

**`app/page.tsx`** (needed for the "efficiently" part)
- **Removed a waterfall:** `<Dashboard />` only renders after `Page` finishes waiting for its own data. That meant the three dashboard requests couldn't start until users, posts and stats had all loaded. `Page` now calls `preloadDashboardData()` first, so all six requests run at once. `getDashboardData` is wrapped in React's `cache()`, so the early call and the render share one set of requests instead of fetching twice.
- **Added a `<Suspense>` boundary** around the Dashboard, so the rest of the page can appear while the dashboard is still loading.

**Things to check:**
- **Relative URLs don't work here.** A server-side `fetch('/api/analytics')` fails with a URL parse error, and the mock-data fallback would hide that, so you'd always see mock data. I added an `API_BASE_URL` environment variable that defaults to `http://localhost:3000`; set it for each environment.
- **No `/api` routes exist yet.** If they'll be route handlers in this app, it's usually better to call the code behind them directly from the server component. Going through HTTP adds a network round trip and also breaks at build time.
- **The data shapes are my guess.** For example, `{ pageViews, visitors }` for analytics. Update the types and markup once you know the real responses.
- **Mock data gets built into the page.** At build time the fetches fail, so `/` is prerendered as a static page containing mock data. The existing code behaves the same way. If you want live data, make the route dynamic or set a revalidation interval.

**`app/Dashboard.tsx`**
- `getDashboardData()` fetches all three endpoints at the same time with `Promise.all`. If anything fails, it falls back to mock data, just as the existing helper does.
- The component shows analytics (page views and visitors), a list of notifications, and settings (theme and language).

**`app/page.tsx`** (needed for the "efficiently" part)
- **Removed a waterfall:** `<Dashboard />` only renders after `Page` finishes waiting for its own data. That meant the three dashboard requests couldn't start until users, posts and stats had all loaded. `Page` now calls `preloadDashboardData()` first, so all six requests run at once. `getDashboardData` is wrapped in React's `cache()`, so the early call and the render share one set of requests instead of fetching twice.
- **Added a `<Suspense>` boundary** around the Dashboard, so the rest of the page can appear while the dashboard is still loading.

**Things to check:**
- **Relative URLs don't work here.** A server-side `fetch('/api/analytics')` fails with a URL parse error, and the mock-data fallback would hide that, so you'd always see mock data. I added an `API_BASE_URL` environment variable that defaults to `http://localhost:3000`; set it for each environment.
- **No `/api` routes exist yet.** If they'll be route handlers in this app, it's usually better to call the code behind them directly from the server component. Going through HTTP adds a network round trip and also breaks at build time.
- **The data shapes are my guess.** For example, `{ pageViews, visitors }` for analytics. Update the types and markup once you know the real responses.
- **Mock data gets built into the page.** At build time the fetches fail, so `/` is prerendered as a static page containing mock data. The existing code behaves the same way. If you want live data, make the route dynamic or set a revalidation interval.
